title: Qian & Sejnowski Feedforward Neural Network Breaks Structural Biology Plateau on Protein Secondary Structure
whyItMatters: First landmark neural network breakthrough in structural biology: Qian & Sejnowski reached 64.3% protein secondary-structure accuracy on unseen proteins, breaking a decade-long statistical ceiling and launching neural protein science.
summary: Published in the Journal of Molecular Biology on August 20, 1988, Ning Qian and Terrence J. Sejnowski at Johns Hopkins University applied backpropagation-trained neural networks to predict alpha-helix, beta-sheet, and coil secondary structure directly from amino-acid sequence windows. Achieving 64.3% three-state accuracy on non-homologous test proteins—beating classical Chou–Fasman and GOR statistical methods that had stalled for over a decade—the paper proved neural networks could extract higher-order local biochemical sequence patterns and directly founded the neural structural-biology lineage culminating in PHD, RaptorX, and AlphaFold.
technicalHighlights: Trained a sliding-window backpropagation neural network (plus a cascaded structure-to-structure refinement network) on 106 crystallized proteins.
Reached 64.3% Q3 accuracy on non-homologous test proteins, surpassing classical Chou–Fasman and GOR informational methods.
Established cascaded two-level neural architectures and direct sequence-to-structure learning as foundations of computational structural biology.
caveats: Predicted 1D secondary structure (helix/sheet/coil) rather than full 3D atomic coordinates, and remained bounded by single-sequence local windows.

scoreRationale.foundational: First major neural network breakthrough in molecular biology, proving learned representations beat hand-crafted statistical potentials.
scoreRationale.ripple: Launched the 32-year neural structural-biology lineage from PHD (1993) to RaptorX (2017) and AlphaFold 2 (2020).
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Journal of Molecular Biology (Vol. 202, pp. 865–884) and independently reproduced across structural bioinformatics.
scoreRationale.velocity: Early neural training on late-1980s workstations.
